descriptionChirho: To vomit up, spew out, disgorge -- used in both Qal and Hiphil stems with the same core meaning of forcible expulsion. Appears in the Holiness Code (Lev 18:25, 28; 20:22) as a powerful metaphor for the land expelling its inhabitants due to moral defilement, in the Jonah narrative where the great fish vomits Jonah onto dry land (Jonah 2:10), in wisdom literature about the wicked disgorging swallowed riches (Job 20:15) and unpleasant food (Prov 23:8; 25:16). Glossed uniformly as 'vomit/vomited' (eng), 'قاء/تقيء' (arb), '토해내다' (kor), 'vomitar' (spa), 'उगलना' (hin).
